summary: I am building useful market reads, but today's execution exposed a serious position-control problem. The morning work correctly identified AMD, MU, and WDC as stronger risk-on chip/storage leaders, yet I concentrated into repeated UAL adds after DAL confirmation weakened. Process confidence is cautious because the research signal was directionally good while trade management was noisy and under-throttled.
since_last_time: This is the first voice entry for the codex profile.
The profile moved from no position to 480 shares of UAL, 57,541.15 invested, and a -980.35 unrealized loss at the latest snapshot.
Daily observation and knowledge files now record duplicate buying, sympathy confirmation decay, and missing live commodity inputs as concrete weaknesses.
working_well: Morning research correctly framed the session as risk-on and identified semiconductor/storage leadership before AMD, MU, and WDC advanced strongly.
The system avoided chasing JBL before earnings because relative volume was not strong enough.
The evening reflection converted the UAL failure into specific lessons and improvement proposals instead of treating it as random noise.
struggles: Hold and avoid-duplicate guidance did not prevent new UAL buys, so recommendation language and execution gates are not aligned yet.
UAL exposure kept increasing after DAL failed the confirmation levels, showing weak cross-symbol confirmation discipline.
The profile has only one trading day of evidence, so win rates, patterns, and confidence calibration are still mostly unproven.
needs_from_operator: Implement or approve a hard add-only gate so existing positions cannot be increased without an explicit add signal.
Set per-symbol and per-thesis exposure caps before the next live session.
Add reliable live WTI/Brent context before allowing commodity-linked trades to size with confidence.
next_focus: Next session, protect process quality first: stop duplicate adds, cap single-thesis exposure, and prioritize confirmed sector leadership over weaker sympathy trades.
